statement: A tank measures 1.2 m by 50 cm by 40 cm. A tap pours 200 cm^3 of water into it every second. How many minutes does the tap take to fill the empty tank?

choices.misconception: I changed 1.2 m into 12 cm instead of 120 cm.
I changed 1.2 m into 1200 cm instead of 120 cm.
I found the time in seconds and forgot to change it into minutes.
I found 1200 seconds and then multiplied by 60 instead of dividing.

hints: Put all three lengths in the same unit first.
Work in centimetres, because the tap's rate is in cubic centimetres. Find the volume, divide by the rate, and then check which time unit the question wants.
The tank is 120 cm by 50 cm by 40 cm. Dividing its volume by 200 gives seconds, not minutes.

solutions.reliable: In centimetres the tank is 120 by 50 by 40, so its volume is 240 000 cm^3. At 200 cm^3 per second it takes 240 000 / 200 = 1200 seconds. There are 60 seconds in a minute, so that is 1200 / 60 = 20 minutes. The transferable idea: convert to one unit before multiplying, and re-read which unit the answer needs.
solutions.elegant: 200 cm^3 per second is 12 000 cm^3, or 12 litres, per minute, and the tank holds 240 litres, so it takes 240 / 12 = 20 minutes.

whyOnTest: Checking units and re-reading before bubbling: mixed length units and a per-second rate test whether you convert before multiplying and answer in the unit asked for.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
